---
title: "P4 exercise — Distinguish signal from mechanism"
---

Allow about 60 minutes using the [tutorial](index.qmd). All treatment results
below are invented teaching observations. The aim is to build explanations and
identify experiments that discriminate between them; no wet-lab procedure is
specified here.

## 1. Draw a response chain

A seedling bends towards unilateral blue light. Draw cue → perception →
unequal cellular response → organ curvature. Name a relevant receptor class
and distinguish the signalling role of light from its energy contribution.
Propose controls for gravity, handling and general loss of seedling vigour.

## 2. A hormone rescue is informative but limited

An invented dwarf line is short without added gibberellin and approaches the
untreated wild-type height with added hormone. Untreated wild type is taller
than untreated dwarf; hormone-treated wild type is taller still. Suggest a
defect compatible with these observations and one unsupported conclusion.
What would a failure to respond to hormone suggest, and why would uptake or
dosage still need checking?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Separate synthesis from response

Rescue is compatible with inadequate hormone production, but an external
treatment can bypass several upstream problems. A phenotype plus rescue does
not identify a specific mutated gene.
:::

## 3. Count germination correctly

Each of four independently prepared dishes contains 20 seeds. At day five,
control dishes show 12 and 14 radicle emergences; treated dishes show 16 and
18. Calculate percentages for each dish and the mean within each group.
What must be true about treatment assignment for dishes to be independent
treatment units? Explain why non-germinated seeds cannot all be labelled dead.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Arithmetic check

Control dishes: 60% and 70%, mean 65%. Treated dishes: 80% and 90%, mean 85%.
The descriptive difference is 20 percentage points. The sample is only two
dishes per condition; no general mechanistic or inferential claim follows
from the percentages alone.
:::

## 4. Evaluate a mobile flowering signal

Read the abstract of [Corbesier and colleagues' primary study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17446353/).
Identify the species, proposed moving signal and two kinds of evidence used.
Why is detecting a protein in a receiver region more informative about movement
than measuring only flowering time? Why does a tagged construct need functional
controls? Distinguish expression of the gene from movement of its product.

## 5. Interpret reproductive and ageing outcomes

Two groups make equal flower numbers, but one makes fewer viable seeds.
List three stages after flower initiation that could account for the difference.
Then compare normal leaf senescence with sudden tissue damage: what time-course,
nutrient-remobilisation or contextual evidence would help distinguish them?
Do not use yellow colour alone as a decisive mechanism test.

## Completion check

Your explanations should connect signalling to cell behaviour and distinguish
germination, establishment, flowering, fertilisation and seed production.
Complete the [self-check](quiz.qmd).
